mainTopic: Three ברייתות on moving a שופר and חצוצרות on שבת matched to three תנאים, and lists of names that switched over time (רב חסדא, אביי, רב אשי)
overview: The גמרא is in the middle of explaining contradictory ברייתות about whether one may move a שופר or חצוצרות on שבת. It first challenges the earlier split between a private and a communal שופר. A communal שופר can also feed a poor child, and a third ברייתא allows moving even trumpets. It then answers that each ברייתא follows a different תנא: רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון, or רבי נחמיה. To fix a wording problem in the ברייתא of רבי נחמיה, it quotes רב חסדא, who taught that three pairs of names switched after the בית המקדש was destroyed: שופר and חצוצרות, ערבה and צפצפה, and two words for a table. Each switch has a practical difference (נפקא מינה): the שופר of ראש השנה, the לולב, and buying and selling. אביי adds that the names of two animal stomachs switched, which matters for a needle found in the stomach wall in the laws of טריפות. Finally, רב אשי adds that the city names בבל and בורסיף switched.

steps.title: A communal שופר can also be used for a poor child
steps.stepSummary: אביי attacks רב יוסף's private/communal distinction. A communal שופר can also be used to give water to a poor child, so it has a permitted use too.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A private שופר is fit to pour water with] for a child. But a communal שופר is also fit to pour water for a poor child!
steps.whatsHappening: The first word finishes the previous idea: a private שופר may be moved because it can be used to give water to a baby. Right away, אביי challenges this by saying a communal שופר could feed a poor baby too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had said a private שופר may be moved and a communal one may not. The reason given was that a private שופר has a permitted use: feeding a child through its narrow mouth. אביי points out that the community supports poor children, so a communal שופר has that same permitted use, and the distinction collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: a baby / small child
the community; here, a שופר owned by the community
to give someone a little to drink, sip by sip
a poor person

steps.confusionAlert: The first word, לתינוק, is not the start of a new idea. It is the last word of the previous sentence about a private שופר.

phrases.notes: End of the previous statement: a private shofar is fit to pour water with for a child.

phrases.english: it is fit to give drink to a poor child!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּצִיבּוּר נָמֵי, חֲזֵי לְגַמֵּעַ לְתִינוֹק עָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer from the previous daf, which separated a private שופר from a communal one.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's distinction between a private and a communal שופר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason a private שופר is allowed (feeding a child) applies equally to a communal שופר, because the community feeds poor children.

steps.title: A third ברייתא allows moving both
steps.stepSummary: A further problem: a third ברייתא says that just as you may move a שופר, you may move חצוצרות. Whose view is that?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, what about that which was taught: Just as one may move a שופר, so too one may move trumpets. Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a second problem. A third ברייתא allows moving even trumpets, and none of the ideas so far explains that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, one ברייתא allowed a שופר but not חצוצרות, and another forbade both. Now a third allows both. Since a trumpet has no permitted use, the private/communal approach cannot explain this ruling, so the גמרא asks which תנא could hold it.

keyTerms.meaning: and furthermore; adds another difficulty
we may move (an object on שבת)
trumpets
whose view is it?

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which was taught in a baraita:
Just as one may move the shofar,
so too one may move the trumpets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second difficulty on top of the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to settle the ברייתות with the private/communal distinction
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A third ברייתא permits even trumpets, which have no permitted use, so no explanation offered so far accounts for it.

steps.title: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: New answer: the three ברייתות follow three תנאים. The ruling allowing שופר but not חצוצרות is רבי יהודה's, the ruling allowing both is רבי שמעון's, and the ruling forbidding both is רבי נחמיה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult: this one is רבי יהודה, this one is רבי שמעון, this one is רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The private/communal answer is dropped. Instead, each ברייתא is matched to a different תנא's view on מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds the rules of מוקצה apply. A שופר has a permitted use (feeding a child), so it may be moved, but a trumpet has none and may not be moved. רבי שמעון does not apply מוקצה here, so both may be moved. רבי נחמיה holds a utensil may be used only for its main purpose, so neither may be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: rather; signals dropping the old answer for a new one
it is not difficult
תנא who limits use of a utensil to its main purpose

steps.whatToRemember: Three ברייתות correspond to three views: רבי יהודה (שופר yes, חצוצרות no), רבי שמעון (both yes), רבי נחמיה (both no).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the ברייתות do not truly contradict each other. They reflect a real three-way מחלוקת about מוקצה.

phrases.notes: Shofar may be moved, trumpets may not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both difficulties by replacing רב יוסף's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different tanna (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All the ברייתות follow one view and must be reconciled by a difference in case (private vs. communal).
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא: רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון, and רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: In this ברייתא, 'שופר' means trumpets
steps.stepSummary: This answers an unspoken question. Under רבי נחמיה, why would the ברייתא mention both שופר and חצוצרות? The answer is that its word 'שופר' refers to trumpets, following רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is 'שופר'? Also trumpets, in line with רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes a small wording problem in the ברייתא it assigned to רבי נחמיה. It explains that the word 'שופר' there actually means trumpets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a שופר may not be moved, then obviously a trumpet may not be moved, so mentioning both seems unnecessary. The גמרא answers that the names were switched in later times, so the word 'שופר' in this ברייתא refers to trumpets. The source for this is רב חסדא, quoted next.

keyTerms.meaning: and what is...? (asks what a word means)
in line with רב חסדא's statement

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles a wording difficulty created by assigning a ברייתא to רבי נחמיה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שופר' in the ברייתא means an actual ram's horn, so listing trumpets too is redundant.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שופר' in that ברייתא refers to trumpets, because the names switched.

steps.title: רב חסדא: three names switched after the Temple was destroyed
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that three objects swapped names after the חורבן. The first pair is that what was called a trumpet came to be called a שופר, and the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said: These three things had their names changed since the בית המקדש was destroyed: 'trumpet' became 'שופר,' and 'שופר' became 'trumpet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב חסדא as the source for the name-swap idea it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא lists three pairs of words that swapped meanings after the בית המקדש was destroyed. The first pair, שופר and חצוצרות, directly supports the reading in the previous step. The other two pairs come next.

keyTerms.meaning: three things
their names were changed
the Temple was destroyed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the reinterpretation in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That 'שופר' in the ברייתא can mean trumpets
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's statement that the names of שופר and חצוצרות switched after the חורבן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, the names of three objects switched, starting with שופר and חצוצרות.

steps.title: Practical difference: the שופר of ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the name swap matters in practice. It matters for the שופר of ראש השנה: one must know which modern name refers to the real שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference? For the שופר of ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference the name change makes, and answers that it matters for ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ראש השנה the מצוה can only be done with a real שופר. Since the names swapped, someone asking today for the right instrument must be told its new name, a 'trumpet,' so he does not end up with the wrong object.

keyTerms.meaning: what practical difference does it make?
the New Year, when the מצוה of blowing שופר applies

phrases.english: For the shofar of Rosh Hashanah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for and supplies the practical result of the first name swap.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why it matters in practice that the names שופר and חצוצרות switched
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It matters for performing the מצוה of שופר on ראש השנה with the correct instrument.

steps.title: Second pair: ערבה and צפצפה
steps.stepSummary: Second item in רב חסדא's list: what was called ערבה came to be called צפצפה, and the reverse.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא's list continues with the second pair of switched names: two similar kinds of willow trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ערבה is the willow used for the ארבע מינים, and a צפצפה is a similar tree that is not valid for the מצוה. After the חורבן, people began calling each one by the other's name.

keyTerms.meaning: willow; one of the ארבע מינים
a similar tree, not valid for the מצוה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב חסדא's list with its second item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names ערבה and צפצפה switched after the חורבן.

steps.title: Practical difference: the לולב
steps.stepSummary: The ערבה name swap matters for the מצוה of לולב (the ארבע מינים), which requires a real ערבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference? For the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: Again the גמרא asks what practical difference the name change makes. The answer is the מצוה of לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארבע מינים, called 'לולב' after their main species, require a true ערבה and not a צפצפה. One must know which modern name refers to the valid tree.

keyTerms.meaning: palm branch; also used as a name for the whole מצוה of the ארבע מינים

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the practical result of the second name swap.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ערבה/צפצפה name swap matters
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the מצוה of לולב, which requires a true ערבה.

steps.title: Third pair: two words for a table
steps.stepSummary: Third item in רב חסדא's list: פתורא (originally a large table) and פתורתא (originally a small table) swapped names.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא's list ends with the third pair: two words for tables of different sizes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Originally פתורא meant a big table and פתורתא meant a small one. After the חורבן, the meanings flipped.

keyTerms.meaning: originally, a large table
originally, a small table

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב חסדא's list with its third and final item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names for a large and a small table switched after the חורבן.

steps.title: Practical difference: buying and selling
steps.stepSummary: The table name swap matters for מקח וממכר: an order for a 'פתורא' today means a small table.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference? For buying and selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last practical difference. The table name swap matters in business deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sale, words are understood the way people use them now. So someone who orders a 'פתורא' today receives a small table and cannot demand a large one.

keyTerms.meaning: buying and selling; commercial transactions

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: after the חורבן, three pairs of names switched: שופר/חצוצרות (matters for ראש השנה), ערבה/צפצפה (matters for לולב), and פתורא/פתורתא (matters for buying and selling). This switch also explains why the ברייתא following רבי נחמיה uses the word 'שופר' for trumpets.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the practical result of the third name swap and completes רב חסדא's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the table name swap matters
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For commercial transactions, where words are understood by their current meaning.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three name swaps have practical results, and the first one explains the wording of the ברייתא that follows רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: אביי adds a name swap: two stomachs of an animal
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds his own example to רב חסדא's list: the stomach once called הובלילא is now called בי כסי, and the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We too can say such a thing. What used to be called הובלילא is now called בי כסי, and what used to be called בי כסי is now called הובלילא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues the pattern of רב חסדא and gives a new example from his own generation: the names of two stomachs of an animal swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא listed name swaps that happened after the חורבן. אביי, a later אמורא, says the same thing happened in his time. This time the swap is between the first stomach (הובלילא) and the second stomach (בי כסי) of an animal that chews its cud.

keyTerms.meaning: We too shall say: a way of adding a new example to an earlier list
Originally the name of the first stomach of a cud-chewing animal
Originally the name of the second stomach (the honeycomb-like stomach)

phrases.english: Abaye said: We too shall say:
What was called 'huvlila' is now called 'bei kasei',
phrases.notes: The first stomach now goes by the second stomach's name.

phrases.english: and what was called 'bei kasei' is now called 'huvlila'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new item to the list of name swaps begun by רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names הובלילא and בי כסי swapped in אביי's generation.

steps.title: Why the stomach name swap matters: a needle in the stomach wall
steps.stepSummary: The swap matters for טריפות: a needle stuck in the thick wall of the second stomach makes the animal a טריפה only if it goes through both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? It matters for a needle found in the thick wall of the second stomach (בית הכוסות). If the needle shows on only one side, the animal is kosher. If it shows on both sides, the animal is a טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as with רב חסדא's examples, the גמרא asks what practical difference the swap makes, and answers that it matters for the laws of טריפות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second stomach has a thick wall, so a needle that pierces only one side does not make the animal a טריפה. A needle through both sides does make it a טריפה. Since the first stomach has a different rule, a שוחט must know which modern name means the real 'second stomach' that the הלכה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference?
The second stomach (Hebrew name for בי כסי)
Thickness: here, the thick wall of the stomach
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
Kosher, permitted

steps.confusionAlert: The names swapped, so the old texts' 'בית הכוסות' is what people in אביי's time called הובלילא. The rule follows the real stomach, not the current name.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a real כשרות question that comes up in בדיקת טריפות; using the wrong name could cause a kosher animal to be called a טריפה or the reverse.

phrases.english: For a needle found in the thick wall of the second stomach,
where if it pierced from one side, the animal is kosher,
but if from both sides, it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical effect of אביי's name swap.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does it matter which stomach is called by which name?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule for a needle in the thick wall of the second stomach (kosher if one side, treif if both sides) depends on identifying the correct stomach.

steps.title: רב אשי adds a name swap: בבל and בורסיף
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds a final example: the cities called בבל and בורסיף swapped names.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We too can say such a thing. What used to be called בבל is now called בורסיף, and what used to be called בורסיף is now called בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי, an even later אמורא, adds one more example to the list: two city names swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the swap is about place names, not objects or body parts. The גמרא does not spell out a practical difference here.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylon: originally the name of one city
Bursif: a nearby city whose name swapped with בבל

steps.whatToRemember: Names can change over time. רב חסדא, אביי and רב אשי each show that the הלכה is attached to the actual object (the real שופר, the real ערבה, the real second stomach), so one must know which name refers to it today. In buying and selling, words are understood by their current meaning.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אַף אָנוּ נֹאמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: We too shall say:
What was called 'Bavel' is now called 'Bursif',
and what was called 'Bursif' is now called 'Bavel'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אַף אָנוּ נֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last item to the running list of name swaps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names בבל and בורסיף swapped in later generations.
